doc.title: Paul Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999

title: Auditioning for Ozzie Nelson and Rasputin's Laundry
summary: In 1941 he joined Ozzie Nelson's dance band and wrote a Lunceford-style chart that made the audience gather round; Ozzie later recalled it when Ricky Nelson recorded.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Yeah I did pretty well what I wanted to do, and I mean getting back to 1941, I don’t really remember how it happened, but I had a chance to audition for Ozzie Nelson. And I went up and played and he liked the way I played, and the thing I think that made me stay with the band, you know I wrote an arrangement for him. And Ozzie had always had one of those Dick Jurgens type bands, I mean the people danced and it was a nice dance band and he had a style where the baritone player was always roving around on the bass clef while the band was playing, I mean that was kind of the distinctive style of the band, but it was kind of a dull band from a standpoint of swinging or anything you know. I wrote a thing for him called “Rasputin’s Laundry.” It’s a great title you know. This was in 1941. But it was a Lunceford type thing.

Yeah. Just a thing I whipped up, you know [scats] but the dotted eighths and sixteenths that Lunceford used to play. And he broke it in at Evichen’s Garden up in Denver. And for the first time in his history, the audience gathered around the bandstand and clapped at the end of the thing instead of just dancing around like they usually did. And his statement to me, he said, “I don’t understand the music,” but he said, “write some more like that.”
Oh, that’s great. It almost sounds like a little movie scene.

And ironically I did Ricky’s first record with Ozzie in the booth. And when Ricky did his first tune Ozzie turned to me and he said, “now you know how I felt about your writing.” © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-

Because he didn’t know what Ricky was doing with the rock scene. I mean Ozzie was totally out of that you know. And he said that was the same feeling he had when that “Rasputin’s Laundry” came to this band.
He was a bit mystified but he knew if it was working though I guess.
